/-!
# Conjecture 5.39

by P. M. Neumann

Prove that every countable group can act faithfully as a group of automorphisms of a
finitely generated soluble group (of derived length at most $4$).

A group $H$ acts faithfully as a group of automorphisms of $G$ exactly when there is an
injective group homomorphism $H \to \operatorname{Aut}(G)$, i.e. when $H$ is isomorphic to
a subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$. Finite groups are countable, so they are included.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), problem 5.39.
- P. M. Neumann, *in: Groups–Korea, Pusan, 1988* (Lect. Notes Math. **1398**), Springer,
  Berlin, 1989, 124–139 (background, including the relationship with problem 8.50).
-/

blocks.docstring:
Stronger form: every countable group $H$ can act faithfully as a group of automorphisms of a
finitely generated soluble group of derived length at most $4$, i.e. there is a finitely
generated group $G$ with $G^{(4)} = 1$ and an injective group homomorphism
$H \to \operatorname{Aut}(G)$. Here $G^{(0)} = G$ and $G^{(n+1)} = [G^{(n)}, G^{(n)}]$, so
`derivedSeries G 4 = ⊥` already implies that $G$ is soluble.

claims.decomposer_note: Prop: for every countable group H (finite groups included; no nontriviality assumed) there exist a finitely generated (Group.FG) soluble (IsSolvable) group G and an injective group homomorphism H →* MulAut G (H isomorphic to a subgroup of Aut G); the converse is trivial since Aut of an f.g. group is countable, and the cited Neumann paper / problem 8.50 is background only and poses no further question.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates encode the same faithful statement: for every H with [Group H] [Countable H] (finite/trivial groups included, as 'every countable group' intends) there exist G : Type, Group G, Group.FG G, IsSolvable G, and an injective φ : H →* MulAut G (MulAut G = G ≃* G = Aut G for a group). c04 chosen for style: hypothesis-style binders, universe-polymorphic H : Type*, and a module docstring citing the Neumann background paper. Verified against Mathlib source that IsSolvable/Group.FG/derivedSeries have the expected meaning; no degenerate boundary cases (trivial H only makes that instance trivially true).
claims.source_text: Prove that every countable group can act faithfully as a group of automorphisms of a finitely generated soluble group
claims.text_span:

claims.decomposer_note: Stronger form of the primary claim: the f.g. soluble group G can moreover be taken of derived length ≤ 4, i.e. derivedSeries G 4 = ⊥ in Mathlib's convention (derivedSeries G 0 = ⊤), which already implies IsSolvable; the parenthetical is a sharpening, not a separate co-equal question.
claims.reviewer_why: Encodes 'derived length ≤ 4' as derivedSeries G 4 = ⊥, exact under Mathlib's convention derivedSeries G 0 = ⊤ with descending series; checked in Lean that this implies IsSolvable G, so omitting the redundant IsSolvable witness (as c03–c08 do) is correct and cleaner than c01/c02's duplication. Same faithful f.g. + injective-embedding structure as the main slot.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The split into the main claim (f.g. soluble) and the parenthetical sharpening (derived length ≤ 4) matches the source text.

/-!
# Conjecture 5.39

by P. M. Neumann

Prove that every countable group can act faithfully as a group of automorphisms of a
finitely generated soluble group (of derived length at most $4$).

A group $H$ acts faithfully as a group of automorphisms of $G$ exactly when there is an
injective group homomorphism $H \to \operatorname{Aut}(G)$, i.e. when $H$ is isomorphic to
a subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$. Finite groups are countable, so they are included.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), problem 5.39.
- P. M. Neumann, *in: Groups–Korea, Pusan, 1988* (Lect. Notes Math. **1398**), Springer,
  Berlin, 1989, 124–139 (background, including the relationship with problem 8.50).
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.39»

/--
Every countable group $H$ can act faithfully as a group of automorphisms of a finitely
generated soluble group: there is a finitely generated soluble group $G$ and an injective
group homomorphism $H \to \operatorname{Aut}(G)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.39» (H : Type*) [Group H] [Countable H] :
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Group.FG G ∧ IsSolvable G ∧
      ∃ φ : H →* MulAut G, Function.Injective φ := by
  sorry

/--
Stronger form: every countable group $H$ can act faithfully as a group of automorphisms of a
finitely generated soluble group of derived length at most $4$, i.e. there is a finitely
generated group $G$ with $G^{(4)} = 1$ and an injective group homomorphism
$H \to \operatorname{Aut}(G)$. Here $G^{(0)} = G$ and $G^{(n+1)} = [G^{(n)}, G^{(n)}]$, so
`derivedSeries G 4 = ⊥` already implies that $G$ is soluble.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.39».variants.derived_length_le_four (H : Type*) [Group H] [Countable H] :
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Group.FG G ∧ derivedSeries G 4 = ⊥ ∧
      ∃ φ : H →* MulAut G, Function.Injective φ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.39»

items: Faithful action as a group of automorphisms is modelled as an injective group homomorphism H →* MulAut G (equivalently, H isomorphic to a subgroup of Aut G), rather than via a MulDistribMulAction with FaithfulSMul; these are equivalent.

The acting group H is universe-polymorphic (Type*) while the f.g. group G is existentially quantified in Type; this loses no generality because a finitely generated group is countable and so can be realised in Type 0.
Derived length ≤ 4 is encoded as derivedSeries G 4 = ⊥ using Mathlib's derivedSeries (G^{(0)} = G, G^{(n+1)} = [G^{(n)}, G^{(n)}]); IsSolvable is not repeated in the variant since it follows.

The statement is imperative ('Prove that…'), so it is stated as a direct proposition (no answer(sorry)), per CONTRIBUTING.md. No nontriviality hypothesis on H is imposed; trivial/finite H are included as in the source.
The Neumann 1989 Groups–Korea reference and problem 8.50 are cited in the module docstring as background only; they pose no further formal content.

reviewer_notes: All candidates were mathematically identical and faithful; differences were purely stylistic (∀ vs hypothesis binders, Type vs Type*, redundant IsSolvable in the variant). Final file is c04 with light docstring edits; it compiles with only 'declaration uses sorry' warnings. Modeling notes: 'act faithfully as a group of automorphisms' = injective hom into MulAut G (equivalent to a faithful MulDistribMulAction); the problem is imperative ('Prove that…') so stated as a plain proposition without answer(sorry); G is existentially quantified in Type (no loss: an f.g. group is countable); the Neumann 1989 paper and problem 8.50 are background only and pose no additional formal content. The parenthetical 'of derived length at most 4' is shipped as the sharpening variant per the decomposition table; both slots are stated.
